faq.q: Why is potassium at the top?
faq.a: Potassium loses its single outer electron very easily, so it reacts faster than any other common metal, even bursting into flame on water.
asks: What is the most reactive metal?

faq.q: Why does copper not react with acid?
faq.a: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot push hydrogen out of an acid. That makes it good for water pipes.
asks: Why are pipes made of copper?

faq.q: Why is gold found as pure metal?
faq.a: Gold is so unreactive that it does not join with oxygen or other elements in the ground. So it is found as nuggets or flakes of pure metal.
The reactivity series is a list of metals in order of how readily they react, from the most reactive, like potassium, to the least reactive, like gold.

faq.q: How can you work out the reactivity series?
faq.a: Watch how fast metals react with water or dilute acid. The faster the fizzing, the more reactive the metal. Displacement reactions also show the order.
asks: Experiment to find the reactivity series

facts: A common reactivity series is potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium, (carbon), zinc, iron, (hydrogen), copper, silver, gold.
Metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series react with dilute acids to produce hydrogen.
